title: At the Doctor's
sourceNote: The auto-captions are heavily garbled; the vocabulary and the phone dialogue were reconstructed from context and standard German. The doctor and patient phrases follow the teacher's list as closely as the captions allow; a few extra phrases are marked as additions.
objectives: I can make a doctor's appointment on the phone
I can describe my symptoms to a doctor
I can understand the doctor's questions and simple advice
I can use the key words for medicine and prescriptions

grammar.title: Masculine and feminine job words
grammar.body: Most job words have a masculine and a feminine form. Feminine forms add **-in**, the plural adds **-nen**: **der Arzt – die Ärztin**, **der Patient – die Patientin**. Plurals: *die Ärzte, die Ärztinnen, die Patienten, die Patientinnen*.

grammar.title: den Patienten: a small surprise
grammar.body: The teacher says: the doctor examines **den Patienten** (not *den Patient*). Here *Patient* gets an extra **-en** in the accusative. You will learn why later; for now just memorise the phrase **Der Arzt untersucht den Patienten.**

grammar.title: Irregular and inseparable verbs
grammar.body: **messen** is irregular: ich messe, du **misst**, er / sie **misst**. **verschreiben** is an inseparable verb (the prefix *ver-* stays on the verb); its participle is **verschrieben**. In the Perfekt: *Der Arzt hat den Blutdruck gemessen.*

grammar.title: Use Sie with the doctor
grammar.body: Always use the **Sie**-form with the doctor and with the staff in the surgery. Address a female doctor as **Frau Doktor** or **Frau Dr. Lampert**.
grammar.ar: مع الطبيب نستخدم دائماً صيغة Sie الرسمية.

grammar.title: Insurance card and sick note
grammar.body: Everyone in Germany has an insurance card (**die Versichertenkarte**). Take it with you to the doctor. If you cannot go to work, the doctor can give you a sick note: **die Arbeitsunfähigkeitsbescheinigung**, often called **die Krankschreibung**.

mistakes.why: *messen* changes e to i in du- and er-form.

lines.de: Guten Tag, Florian Müller hier. Ich möchte einen Termin vereinbaren.
lines.en: Good day, this is Florian Müller. I would like to make an appointment.
I have a sore throat and a cough.

lines.de: Guten Tag, was kann ich für Sie tun?
lines.en: Good day, what can I do for you?

lines.de: Guten Tag, Frau Doktor. Ich fühle mich nicht wohl. Ich habe Kopfschmerzen und Fieber.
lines.en: Good day, doctor. I do not feel well. I have a headache and a fever.

lines.de: Ich messe Ihre Temperatur und Ihren Blutdruck. Der Blutdruck ist normal. Sie haben eine Grippe.
lines.en: I will measure your temperature and your blood pressure. Your blood pressure is normal. You have the flu.

lines.de: Ich schreibe Ihnen ein Rezept. Trinken Sie viel Tee und bleiben Sie im Bett.
lines.en: I will write you a prescription. Drink a lot of tea and stay in bed.

lines.de: Vielen Dank, Frau Doktor. Auf Wiedersehen!
lines.en: Thank you very much, doctor. Goodbye!

tip: Before you go to the doctor, review lesson 43 (being ill) so you can name your symptoms. Always make an appointment first, even when you feel very sick.

summary: Ask for an appointment: Ich möchte einen Termin vereinbaren. Say your symptoms with Ich habe ...
Arzt / Ärztin and Patient / Patientin: feminine forms end in -in, plural -innen.
The doctor examines (untersuchen), measures (messen: er misst) and prescribes (verschreiben).
Key words: Tablette, Kapsel, Tropfen, Salbe, Rezept, Medikament.
Use Sie, and bring your Versichertenkarte. A sick note is a Krankschreibung.
